message.content:
Lions (Panthera leo) belong to the order **Carnivora** (family Felidae), while zebras (Equus quagga) belong to the order **Perissodactyla** (family Equidae).  
Both of those orders are part of the larger clade **Laurasiatheria**, which also contains orders such as Artiodactyla (even‑toed ungulates), Chiroptera (bats), Cetartiodactyla (whales, hippos, etc.), and others.

Therefore, the most recent common ancestor of a lion and a zebra is the last common ancestor of the clade **Laurasiatheria**.  
This ancestor lived roughly **90–100 million years ago** in the Late Cretaceous, before the diversification of the major Laurasiatherian lineages.
